1. 1. This matter is taken up through Hybrid Arrangement (Virtual /Physical Mode).
2. Heard learned counsel for the Petitioners as well as learned Additional Standing Counsel for the State.
Perused the records.

3. This is an application under Section 482 BNSS, 2023 filed by the Petitioners for anticipatory bail,
involving offence punishable under Sections 420,406/34 of the Indian Penal Code.

4. It is stated by the learned counsel for the Petitioners that as per the F.I.R. allegation, the Petitioners had sold some properties belonging to the Church in the year 2022 which was less than the market value.
He further contended that two years after the alleged transaction the F.I.R. has been registered in the year 2024 making false allegation against the present Petitioners.
Learned counsel for the Petitioners further contended that the informant who has been expelled from the Church Council has lodged this F.I.R. against the Petitioners making false allegation.
He also contended that the Petitioners do not have any criminal antecedent and that since they belong to the locality, there is no chance of their absconding.
On such ground, learned counsel for the Petitioners submitted that the Petitioners be released on bail on such terms and conditions as this Court deems just and proper.

5. Learned Additional Standing Counsel on the other hand objected to the release of the Petitioners on pre- arrest bail on the ground seriousness and gravity of the allegation.
Further, it is contended that in the event this Court is inclined to release the Petitioners on bail, then stringent conditions be imposed.

6. Considering the seriousness of the allegation, gravity of the offence and the fact of the case, the Petitioners are directed to surrender and move an application for bail before the learned S.D.J.M.,
Gunupur in G.R.Case No.367 of 2024 arising out of Gunupur P.S.Case No.197 of 2024 within a period of three weeks from today.

In such eventuality, learned court in seisin over the matter shall release the Petitioners on bail on such terms and conditions as the learned Magistrate may deem just and proper in the facts and circumstances of the case, but subject to verification of criminal antecedent.
In the event it is found that the Petitioners are having any criminal antecedent of similar nature, this order shall not be given effect to.
Violation of conditions shall entail cancellation of bail.
7. The ABLAPL is disposed of accordingly.

8. Issue urgent certified copy of this order as per Rules.
( ADITYA KUMAR MOHAPATRA) JUDGE RKS Location: High Court of Orissa, Cuttack )
